However, the decoding complexity varies significantly by format. `Float32` formats are O(1) per component. `Norm` formats require normalization (O(1)). `BC7` requires block decoding (O(1) per 4x4 block, but higher constant factor). `Cluster` formats require codebook lookup (O(1) if hash map, O(log N) if sorted).

**Memory Complexity:** The memory footprint is directly determined by the selected formats. `VeryHigh` uses the most memory (32-bit floats for all attributes). `VeryLow` uses the least, leveraging `BC7` for color and cluster compression for SH.
**Performance:** Higher quality levels (VeryHigh, High) provide better visual fidelity but require more bandwidth and memory.
Lower levels (Low, VeryLow) reduce bandwidth and memory usage at the cost of visual artifacts, particularly in SH coefficients where cluster compression may introduce quantization errors.
**Strengths:** Simple to implement, provides a clear trade-off curve between quality and resources.
**Limitations:** Discrete quality levels may not allow fine-grained tuning.
Cluster compression for SH may not adapt well to all scene content.
